s1.quote: Antilla Wreck: A German freighter sunk on purpose by its own captain on May 10, 1940 … lays at a max depth of 55ft/16.5m on a sandy bottom … Due to its age, we do not penetrate this wreck

s2.quote: Antilla … is nestled in a sandy bottom at a depth of about 55 feet … Her bow and stern are pretty much intact, boasting lots of coral and sponge growth … penetrating the wreck is not advisable

s3.quote: The Antilla Shipwreck is the largest wreck in the Caribbean … A great site for beginner and intermediate divers … Dive Depth 60 feet

highlights.text: Bow and stern intact with coral and sponge growth

hazards.text: Old, unstable wreck; penetration not advised

summary.text: German freighter scuttled by its own crew in 1940, resting on sand in about 17 m off Palm Beach. Bow and stern are fairly intact and covered in coral and sponges; the wreck is too fragile to enter.

s1.quote: Renaissance Airplanes: Two airplanes sunk on purpose … both lay at a maximum depth of 85ft/26m … Due to the stability of both planes, penetration is permitted

s2.quote: Renaissance Airplanes … There are two planes: a YS-11 and a Convair 240 … at depths ranging from 50 to 80 feet

highlights.text: Two sunken airliners: an intact YS-11 and a broken-up Convair

summary.text: Two airliners, a YS-11 and a Convair, deliberately sunk on sand south of Renaissance Island at roughly 15-26 m. The YS-11 is largely intact and the planes can be partly penetrated.

s1.quote: Aruba is home to about one-third of the total population of the Dutch Caribbean

notDiveSite.reason: Whole island, not a single dive site

s1.quote: Jane Sea Wreck: Venezuelan cement cargo ship sunk as an artificial reef back in 1988 … The bow is at 60ft/18m, the top of the stern is at 45ft/15m and the propeller is at 90ft/28m … penetration is not permitted

s2.quote: Jane C (Jane Sea) … her depths ranging from 50 to 90 feet

s3.quote: The Jane Sea … Sitting upright on a sandy bottom near Barcadera Reef, it lies in 100 feet of water … covered with gorgonians and orange cup coral

highlights.text: Gorgonians and orange cup coral cover the wreck
Sits upright next to a coral reef

hazards.text: Wreck is collapsing; one operator bars penetration

summary.text: Cement freighter sunk in 1988 as an artificial reef, upright on sand beside Barcadera Reef with the bow near 18 m and the propeller around 28 m. Covered in gorgonians and cup coral; boat access only.

s1.quote: The Hole in the Wall is a very popular dive spot, since you can dive with the current past the steep and narrow reef wall … Diver Level Beginner Dive Depth 15-110 feet Site Highlight Easily accessible by shore

s2.quote: Hole in the Wall … Sloping coral wall with lots of life. Reef goes down to a maximum depth of 90ft/30m

highlights.text: Steep, narrow reef wall with lots of life

hazards.text: Current carries divers along the wall to Mangel Halto

summary.text: Shore-accessible drift along a steep, narrow reef wall at Mangel Halto, with the current carrying divers to a sandy channel and a shady beach. Rated suitable for beginners; the reef drops to about 30 m.

s1.quote: Sponge Reef … Home to soft coral ranging from orange elephant ear sponges to purple and yellow tube sponges … Diver Level Beginner Dive Depth 15-80 feet Site Highlight Abundant soft sponge corals

s2.quote: Sponge Reef: A reef filled with different types of colorful sponges … Reef slopes down to a maximum depth of 90ft/28m

highlights.text: Many colorful sponges: elephant ear, tube and vase

summary.text: Sloping reef off Druif Beach crowded with colorful sponges, with turtles often passing. Depths run from the shallows down to about 25-28 m; rated beginner-friendly.

s1.quote: Harbor Reef/Tugboat: A gentle sloping reef with a lot of soft corals with patches of hard corals and a sunken tugboat which was sunk in the 1980’s at a maximum depth of 90ft/30m

s2.quote: Harbor Tugboat … Located right off the cruise-ship port in about 80 feet of water is the Harbor Tugboat Wreck … Although small, she is surrounded by a nice reef

highlights.text: Sunken tugboat on a gently sloping soft-coral reef

summary.text: Small sunken tugboat off the cruise-ship port in roughly 25-30 m, set on a gently sloping reef with plenty of soft coral.

s1.quote: The Debbie II, a 120-foot fuel barge, was sunk in 1992 to a depth of 70 feet off the coast of Malmok … divers can get the rest of their fill by exploring Blue Reef nearby
Barcadera Reef … Many brain corals and an abundance of huge sea fans in the shallows … Diver Level Beginner Intermediate Dive Depth 20-80 feet Site Highlight Variety of coral species

s2.quote: Barcadera Reef: Nice hard coral reef area which has slopes going down to a maximum depth of 90ft/28m

highlights.text: Brain corals and huge sea fans in the shallows

summary.text: Hard coral reef near the airport that thins at the entrance and gets denser and richer with depth, running from about 6 m to 25-28 m. Brain corals and big sea fans stand out.

s1.quote: Star Gerren … Holes have been made in the ship to allow easy entry and exit of the wreck … Diver Level Intermediate Dive Depth 60-70 feet Site Highlight Wreck dive, easily accessible by boat

s2.quote: The Star Gerren lies upside down in about 45 to 70 feet of water … holes were cut into the ship to allow divers to safely access the interior

summary.text: German coaster sunk in 2000 off Palm Beach in roughly 14-21 m. Holes were cut in the hull so divers can enter and exit the wreck; reached by boat and rated intermediate.
